scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for English Base Set 2 and twelve rows that carry its reprint-memory, launch-icon, Jungle-blend, trainer-tool, and resource-floor structure.

sources.title: Local English WoC catalog: Base Set 2
Pokemon TCG API v2 set record: Base Set 2
Bulbapedia: Base Set 2 (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API model Base Set 2 as released on February 24, 2000.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API support a 130-row Base Set 2 checklist.
Bulbapedia describes Base Set 2 as composed of reprints from Base Set and Jungle rather than a normal new-mechanics expansion.
The local catalog preserves Base Set 2 as set id base4 and release_family_id en_wotc_base_set_2_20000224, separate from Base Set, Jungle, Shadowless, and First Edition branches.

The local attention rows include Charizard, Blastoise, Venusaur, Mewtwo, Gyarados, Raichu, Scyther, Wigglytuff, Snorlax, Pikachu, Wartortle, and energy / trainer rows that show the compiled set apparatus.
The local Base Set 2 artist clusters are led by Ken Sugimori, Keiji Kinebuchi, Mitsuhiro Arita, and Kagemaru Himeno, reflecting the early visual memory being reassembled rather than newly introduced.

Base Set 2 matters because it shows Pokemon history beginning to curate itself: the launch grammar and Jungle memory are repackaged into one English set, making nostalgia, accessibility, and collector confusion part of the same object.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent memory says Base Set 2, base4, Charizard, Blastoise, Venusaur, Base Set art, Jungle art, Shadowless, First Edition, or same artwork.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Base Set 2 is a 130-row English reprint/compilation release. Preserve set id base4, row number, and Base Set 2 symbol before comparing to Base Set, Jungle, Shadowless, or First Edition copies.
steps: Preserve release_family_id en_wotc_base_set_2_20000224 and Pokemon TCG API set id base4.
Do not treat shared artwork as proof of Base Set, Jungle, Shadowless, First Edition, or original-print identity.
Require the seller scan or graded label to show Base Set 2 symbol / set attribution before carrying a Base Set 2 row into transaction logic.
For price, condition, edition, or authenticity claims, use seller evidence and market evidence; do not infer from catalog memory.
For energy and trainer rows, preserve Base Set 2 row identity even when the name is generic and reused across early sets.

narrative.why_it_matters: Base Set 2 is strange in a useful way. It is not the first spark, and it is not trying to be. It is the early English game learning to package its own memory: Base Set icons, Jungle favorites, familiar trainer tools, and the energy floor gathered into a new object with a new symbol. For a collector, that can feel less pure than a first print. For an agent, it is a perfect lesson: resemblance is not provenance. Same art, different assembly.
